pr_title: server: remove non-deterministic assertion in databasedetails test
pr_body:
This field is non-deterministic. We shouldn't assert that it's 0 as it can return a non-zero value when there is more activity in the cluster.

Epic: none
Fixes: #105504

Release note: None

comments:
I believe @cockroachdb/cluster-observability owns this test failure.

(see https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/103394).

I read the comment here, https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/release-22.2/pkg/server/admin_cluster_test.go#L71-L75, which leads to me believe that this value returning as non-zero in the stress test may not be a bug. This failure has been seen very rarely 22.1 and 22.2 branches which leads me to believe changes in lower layers may have stabilized this test already. I also interpreted it to mean we may be able to remove this check for the 22.2 release branch if we're worried about it returning as non-zero again, but I'll double check before closing.
@matthewtodd it's been a while, but if you have a second to chime in on why we're checking for 0 disk bytes here before I close this, that would be very appreciated!

review_comments:
Let's come back to first principles here: The "Approximate disk bytes" stats is a _very_ important UX outcome for the end-user. If that value is sometimes zero when it shouldn't, or sometimes non-zero when we want it to be zero, that's a real UX + observability bug. If the test is failing non-deterministically here, that's not a problem in the test: it's a problem in the logic, or our understanding of the feature.

There's two possible situations here (I don't know exactly which one is valid):

- the approximate disk bytes should be immediately non-zero after creating the test table above. This is the behavior I expect, especially after @zachlite 's recent changes.  If the test tries to observe zero, and we did the feature right, it's going to fail all the time. 
  In that case maybe the right change is `assert.NotEqual(t, 0, ApproxDiskBytes`)`.

- the approximate disk bytes is somehow computed lazily (we'd need to check with the KV team) so it can be zero for a while until it becomes non-zero.

  In that case the proper fix would be to use `SucceedsSoon` to check that it eventually becomes non-zero. Also in that case I would add some explanation (in a comment) about why the non-zero value lags, i.e. what mechanism in KV is responsible. That also probably deserves a clarifying release note so we properly document it.
